The Honourable Smt. Justice Renuka Yara
 M.A.C.M.A.No.215 of 2023
Judgment:
Heard Sri K. Hari Mohan Reddy, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri N.S.Bhaskar Rao, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the entire record and citations relied upon by the parties.

2. This appeal is filed aggrieved by the order passed by the Chairman, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-XXIV Additional Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad, in M.V.O.P.No.2635 of 2013, dated 05.05.2022, wherein an amount of Rs.2,87,418/- is awarded in a claim petition filed seeking compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the appellant in a road traffic accident.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. The brief facts of the case are that the appellant met with an accident on 05.01.2013 at about 23:30 hours while he was travelling in an auto rickshaw and when the auto rickshaw reached near Sai Sri Tiffin Centre, Kukatpally, a motorcycle bearing No.AP 9 BJ 5694 came in high speed in rash and negligent manner and hit the auto rickshaw.
Due to said accident, the appellant sustained fracture of right leg, head injury and blunt injuries all over the body.
Therefore, claim petition was filed seeking RY,J MACMA_215_2023 compensation of Rs.8,00,000/- and the same was enhanced to Rs.15,00,000/- in view of order passed by this Court in I.A.No.3 of 2023.
4. The appellant got examined P.Ws.1 to 3 and got exhibited Exs.A-1 to A-11.
Respondent No.1-owner and respondent No.2-insurer of the motorcycle involved in the accident did not lead neither oral nor documentary evidence.

On the basis of the evidence adduced by the appellant, the Tribunal passed the impugned award for an amount of Rs.2,87,418/- along with interest at 7.5% per annum leading to filing of the present appeal.

5. In the grounds of appeal, the appellant challenged the quantum of compensation for ignoring disability of 25% which lead to loss of earning capacity at 50% and also failure to award compensation towards loss of amenities, marriage prospects and failure to consider the monthly income of the appellant at Rs.13,000/-.
Further, the Tribunal failed to consider the cost of future surgery though, the same was proven by examining P.W.2 i.e., Dr. P. Mohan Reddy and exhibiting Ex.A-6-estimation certificate.
Hence, prayed that there is need to enhance the compensation.

6. During the arguments in the appeal, it is urged that the Tribunal failed to provide just and fair compensation when there is evidence on record in the form of disability certificate and oral evidence of P.W.2-Dr.P. RY,J MACMA_215_2023 Mohan Reddy, who deposed about the percentage of disability.

In response, learned counsel for respondent No.2 argued that the Tribunal considered the evidence adduced by the appellant in the right perspective and awarded compensation and therefore, there are no grounds to interfere with in the impugned award.

sentences.text:
A perusal of the impugned award shows that while assessing the disability on the basis of the evidence of P.W.2, the Tribunal ventured into unnecessary details as to method of scientific assessment of disability etc., the said portion is extracted and produced below:
"25.
...The petitioner has been relying upon the evidence of PW2 to prove the permanent disability.
PW2 examined the petitioner in the year 2017 where as the petitioner sustained in July in the year 2013.

It is nearly after 4 years of occurrence,
he examined the petitioner.
Further PW2 was not member of medical board when he issued Ex.A5.
PW2 admitted that there is no loss of Rom and muscle strength of hip or right knee joint.

PW2 did not follow any method of scientific assessment of disability and he gave Ex.A5 based on the information regarding difficulty in squatting by the petitioner, that too after 4 years of the accident.
No much reliance can be placed on the evidence of PW2 or Ex.A5.

The petitioner therefore could not establish that he is suffering permanent disability due to injury is sustained in the accident."
8.

The appellant on his part made genuine efforts to prove the disability by examining P.W.2-Dr. P.
Mohan Reddy.
The evidence of P.W.2 shows that he was not only a consultant orthopedic, but also worked as member of medical board at Osmania Hospital.

When such a qualified person RY,J MACMA_215_2023 assessed the disability and issued disability certificate showing the disability at 40%, the same need not be put to unnecessary scrutiny, as the proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, are summary in nature.
Such detailed scrutiny is not required unless there is a serious question about conduct and credibility of the doctor examined.
The record does not disclose any issue about credibility of P.W.2.
Therefore, his evidence about the percentage of disability of the appellant can be considered.

Once the evidence of P.W.2 with respect to percentage of physical disability is considered, the only point to be considered is whether such physical disability would transform into functional disability or not.
9. As per police records, the appellant was a private employee i.e., a relationship manager in IIFL company.
The appellant claims to have monthly income of Rs.13,000/-, but the same was considered at Rs.11,000/- per month by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal awarded Rs.66,000/-
(Rs.11,000/- X 6 months) towards loss of earnings for six months, Rs.6,000/- towards transportation charges, Rs.8,000/- towards extra nourishment, Rs.2,000/- towards damages to the clothing and articles, Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities, social status, marriage prospects,
shock and mental agony, Rs.65,418/- towards medical expenses and Rs.40,000/- towards pain and suffering.
The aforesaid compensation amounts which are awarded under RY,J MACMA_215_2023 various counts are not interfered with.
However, there is need to award compensation towards loss of income due to disability.
10. The appellant was a relationship manager and he may not be able to discharge his duties as prior to the accident.
At the same time, it may not be possible that there is no employment at all for the appellant, as such the functional disability on account of restriction of movement of right knee is taken at 20%.

Further, on the basis of age of the appellant i.e., 25 years at the time of the accident,
40% is added towards future prospects.

After adding 40% of the future prospects, the monthly Dodda Sunil vs V.Murali Krishnam Raju on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165232560/
2 income of the appellant comes to Rs.15,400/-.

sentences.text: Further, as per the judgment in the case of Sarla Varma v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another1, the multiplier that applies to the appellant is 18.

sentences.text:
The loss of income due to disability is calculated as: Rs.15,400/- X 12 X 18 X 20/100 =
Rs.6,65,280/-.
After adding this amount to the compensation granted by the Tribunal under various heads to the appellant, the total amount of compensation comes to Rs.9,52,698/-.

Since the I.A.No.2 of 2023 (condone delay petition) is allowed subject to the appellant/petitioner forgoing interest for the delay period of 64 days in filing the appeal, the appellant is not entitled to claim interest for the delay condoned period of 64 days.
In the result, M.A.C.M.A. is partly allowed.

The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is hereby enhanced from Rs.2,87,418/- to Rs.9,52,698/- with interest at 9% per annum on the enhanced compensation from the date of petition till the date of realization, excluding the delay condoned period of 64 days.
The enhanced compensation amount shall be deposited by the respondents jointly and severally within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
On such deposit, the appellant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount as apportioned by the Tribunal, without furnishing any security.
The appellant shall deposit deficit Court fee, if any.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this appeal, shall stand closed.
